The synthetic OPO world: seeded, stdlib-only, emitting the FIELDS.md vocabulary - donor cases (organ/tissue/both, brain-dead/DCD, complete and in-progress snapshots), referrals, and the eight registers; 59 named plant functions, one per catalog check, each returning the sentence describing what it planted. The generator owns the ground truth; the floor never sees it. The grader and the receipt: every check over every record, compared with ground truth; prints caught/abstained/missed, false-hold rate with its denominator, evaluable coverage per record variant, collateral firings, and the funeral tables; writes RESULTS.md as a fold. SPEC section 12's decider, mechanised at a pinned seed (20260903, 200 cases, 5 plants per check): FAILs if any planted defect passes or the false-hold rate exceeds 1 percent; the generator's own plant invariant surfaces as an instrument FAIL, named as such

New battery law: no check may FIRE on the empty record - a check whose subject is absent must abstain. Graded for all 59. SV-081 and SV-028 given applicability gates (a leading path read that raises when the subject is absent)

what: SPEC section 12's F-FIXTURE is now two mechanical gates: F-FIXTURE (the hand-written battery + DSL/ledger selftests, rung 01's executioner, unchanged) and F-FIXTURE-WORLD (the synthetic world, the section-12 decider)
why: They test different things and the difference is the whole point: the battery grades checks against fixtures written FOR them, the world grades them against records authored without looking at them - and the world found two defects the battery could not see

what: THE APPLICABILITY LAW (candidate LAWS amendment): a check whose subject is absent from the record must ABSTAIN, never fire. Executioner: floor/engine.py grades every check on the empty record; a non-PASS verdict there is a broken check
why: The first run printed a 4.01 percent false-hold rate from exactly two causes, both invisible to hand-written fixtures because a fixture is always written for its check: SV-081 (every conjunct an exists(), which reads absence as False) held every donor chart in the building, and SV-028 (a clock whose completing event never arrives on an organ-only donor, so within()'s as_of fallback treated a never-event as a pending one) alarmed on 17 percent of organ-only records. A check that fires where it does not apply is how a census floor becomes alert fatigue
revert: remove the gate and the two gates in the predicates (not recommended)

what: SV-028 re-anchored from death.pronounced_ts to death.asystole_ts, and every donor record now carries both death.declared_ts and death.asystole_ts
why: Prediction P9, banked before the run and confirmed while modelling the timeline: for a brain-dead donor, death is DECLARED a day or more before circulation stops, and the refrigeration clocks run from asystole (cross-clamp). Anchored to the declaration, the check would have fabricated breaches on every brain-dead organ-and-tissue donor. Fixture pass_anchor_02 plants exactly that error and requires the flip

what: README REV 0 and SPEC REV 0 corrected to REV 1: 'NOTHING HAS RUN' is false as of 2026-09-03; the README leads with the measured result AND with the first run's funeral, and states plainly that F-RETRO has not run
why: Law A6: where a document and a dated receipt disagree, the receipt wins and the document is the defect. The mockup's board numbers stay labelled illustrative (law E2) because F-RETRO is what un-labels them

what: F-FIXTURE-WORLD is graded on a world this project authored; a generator and a floor written by the same hand can share a blind spot. The honest counterweight is a second author for the generator (or a site's real export at rung 04). Should S4 commission an independent generator pass before rung 04, or does F-RETRO subsume it?
